common_name: Otto Quast Spanish Lavender (Compact Rabbit-Ear Lavender)

planting.note: Plant container-grown transplants in fall in extremely well-drained, alkaline to neutral, lean, sandy or gravelly soil in full sun; perfect drainage matters more than any other factor for this cultivar.

directions: Plant in extremely well-drained, lean, alkaline to neutral, sandy or gravelly soil in full sun; like other Spanish lavenders, Otto Quast tolerates Gulf Coast heat and humidity far better than English lavender, but it still fails quickly in wet or heavy clay. This compact, free-flowering selection produces an unusually heavy show of purple flower spikes topped with prominent lavender-pink rabbit-ear bracts, blooming earlier in spring and repeating through the season more reliably than the straight species. Its tidy, rounded habit suits containers, border edges, and rock gardens where taller lavenders would flop. Shear back by about a third after each bloom flush to keep growth dense, and avoid heavy mulch or fertilizer, both of which encourage the rot that kills most garden lavenders.
